Area.evidence_source: Being suicidal is to be in a condition of suffering as the result of important needs not being met. Serious suicide attempts arise from intense psychological pain, which is experienced as unbearable. Hopelessness is considered to be the central emotion associated with suicidality. The perception of being 'trapped in a cage', the lack of a way out, the lack of belief that something or someone can help you and a reduced ability to solve problems on one's own exacerbate the perception of hopelessness and helplessness. ... The aim of this study was to investigate patients' experiences in the aftermath of suicidal crises and what appears to have helped them. ... The attitude and behaviour of healthcare personnel have been reported as alleviating feelings of shame, but they have also been shown to be exacerbative. To be met with respect, listened to, confirmed and given proper time and attention, all of these were reported to be helpful.
